title: Woodshadows floated silently by through the morning peace from the stairhead seaward where he gazed. Inshore and farther out the mirror of water whitened, spurned by lightshod hurrying feet. White breast of the dim sea. The twining stresses, two by two. A hand plucking the harpstrings, merging their twining chords. Wavewhite wedded words shimmering on the dim tide.
html_source:
Stephen is beginning to work on a poem. His mind has left the conflict with Mulligan and has begun to shape, to try to capture in words, a visual impression of the happenstance.

The reference to “lightshod hurrying feet” sounds like a reference to the god Mercury, who, in the Odyssey, is described several times as running over the surface of the ocean with his winged sandals, on his way to deliver messages to mortals.

In the Odyssey this god would have been called Hermes, who in Book 1 at the behest of Athena is dispatched to prompt Calypso to release Odysseus, while she herself goes to Ithaca to stir Telemachus into action. Hermes, like Athena, precipitates change, and here Joyce has combined this Homeric allusion with an image that in itself also suggests change — “the mirror of water whitened”.
